scenes.text: Your brain reacts to a face in a pumpkin almost as fast as to a real face.
Seeing faces in objects is called face pareidolia.
In a two thousand nine study, scientists scanned people looking at face-like objects.
The brain's face area lit up in about one sixth of a second.
Ordinary objects didn't trigger it at all.
So it isn't your imagination playing tricks later. Your brain spots the face right away.
What's the funniest face you've ever seen in an object?

title: Why you see faces in everyday objects 🎃
caption: Face pareidolia: in a 2009 MEG study, face-like objects activated the brain's face-processing area in about 165 ms, almost as fast as real faces. Ordinary objects didn't. 👀
